analysis_trace: Trial NCT06963398 is a Phase 1 first-in-human study of HS-10529, an oral selective KRAS G12D inhibitor by Hansoh Pharma, in advanced solid tumors. The study is NOT_YET_RECRUITING with expected completion April 2029.

Primary endpoint (primary-0) seeks MTD or MAD determination through dose escalation. Evidence from similar KRAS G12D inhibitors (zoldonrasib/RMC-9805, HRS-4642, TSN1611, INCB161734) demonstrates that Phase 1 dose-finding in this class successfully identifies MTD/MAD with manageable safety. Zoldonrasib established RP2D at 1200mg QD; HRS-4642 showed no DLTs in escalation. Evidence role: indirect_direction - supports successful dose identification probability.

Secondary-0 evaluates treatment-emergent adverse events. KRAS G12D inhibitor class shows consistent GI toxicity profile: nausea (~40%), vomiting (~30%), diarrhea (~30%), and rash (~15-18%). Zoldonrasib data (April 2026) showed Grade 3 TRAEs in 13%, no Grade 4/5, 94% dose intensity. Evidence role: indirect_direction - predicts manageable safety profile with class-typical GI AEs.

Secondary-1 measures plasma concentration (PK). Oral small molecule KRAS inhibitors demonstrate dose-proportional PK with measurable exposures. Evidence role: mechanism_background - oral administration and small molecule properties support predictable absorption.
HS-10529 obtained China IND approval April 2025. Hansoh press release indicates good preclinical efficacy, PK, and safety. No human data available yet.

Major uncertainty: No direct clinical data for HS-10529; prediction relies on class extrapolation from competitors (zoldonrasib, HRS-4642). Preclinical-to-clinical translation risk exists. Study early stage (not recruiting) increases execution risk.

Predicted outcomes: MTD/MAD will be identified (high probability given Phase 1 design); AEs will follow class pattern (GI predominant); PK will show measurable exposures. Trial likely to achieve Phase 1 objectives enabling Phase 2 transition.
